title: Steady-state cooperative emission of interlayer excitons in atomically thin light-emitting diodes
authors: Andrés M. Mier Valdivia, Pavel E. Dolgirev, Grace H. Chen, Nadine Leisgang, Andrew Y. Joe, Stefan Ostermann, Deepankur Thureja, Yongxin Zeng, Dapeng Ding, Daniel Rhodes, Bumho Kim, Song Liu, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, James C. Hone, Susanne F. Yelin, Hongkun Park, Mikhail D. Lukin, Philip Kim
abstract: When an ensemble of emitters is confined within an optical wavelength, its radiation can become correlated, leading to cooperative emission. In two-dimensional (2D) transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) electron-hole bilayers, strong light-matter coupling enables the formation of interlayer excitons (IXs), long-lived dipolar excitations that provide an ideal setting for emergent collective phenomena. Here, we engineer an atomically thin light-emitting diode (LED) that generates electroluminescence (EL) from electrically injected IXs that are confined near the sample edges by an edge-enhanced fringing electric field. By measuring Hanbury-Brown-Twiss photon-photon correlations, we find pronounced signatures of collective decay in the form of large photon bunching followed by finite delay antibunching and bunching revivals. These emitter correlation signatures disappear when free charge carriers are doped to form a degenerate Fermi sea but are enhanced by the introduction of localized electrons. The results are consistent with a many-body quantum master equation that models the steady-state superradiant photon statistics of incoherently injected IXs. Our work establishes steady-state cooperative emission in a 2D TMD LED as a platform for studying strong light-matter interactions in electrically driven, non-equilibrium phases of Bose-Fermi mixtures.
summary: This paper reports on the observation of steady-state cooperative emission of interlayer excitons in an atomically thin TMD LED. By measuring photon correlations, the authors confirm superradiant photon statistics, which are highly sensitive to the local charge environment. This work establishes the electrically driven 2D heterostructure as a novel platform for studying strong light-matter interactions.
main_problem: The study investigates the steady-state cooperative emission of interlayer excitons (IXs) in atomically thin light-emitting diodes (LEDs) to probe strong light-matter interactions.
main_result: The experiment observes pronounced photon bunching and complex dynamics in the Hanbury-Brown-Twiss correlations, confirming steady-state superradiant photon statistics in the electrically driven system.
method: The research combines electrical characterization (EL spectroscopy) with advanced photon correlation measurements using a Hanbury-Brown-Twiss interferometer, supported by theoretical modeling.
model_or_system: The physical system is a dual-gated, h-BN encapsulated TMD heterobilayer ($	ext{WSe}_2/	ext{MoSe}_2$) LED. The physics is modeled using a many-body quantum master equation to describe the superradiant photon statistics of incoherently injected IXs.
key_observables: Hanbury-Brown-Twiss photon-photon correlations ($g^{(2)}(	au)$), which show bunching ($g^{(2)}(0) > 2$), antibunching, and revivals; EL intensity and energy shifts; and the dependence of correlations on doping regimes.
important_parameters: The confinement mechanism relies on edge-enhanced fringing electric fields; the system is controlled by bias ($	ext{V}_b$) and gate ($	ext{V}_g$) voltages, which tune the IX charge state ($	ext{IX}^0$, $	ext{IX}^-$ etc.).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the observed correlation signatures arise from steady-state superradiant photon statistics, and the model incorporates an incoherent pumping mechanism.
figures_summary: Figures detail the device structure and band diagram evolution under bias/gate voltage; Figure 2 shows $g^{(2)}(	au)$ measurements across different doping regimes, revealing characteristic bunching dynamics; and Figure 4 presents a model quantitatively reproducing the measured bunching features.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical platform (TMD LED structure and band diagram) by controlling doping via bias/gate voltages. It then measures the key observable ($g^{(2)}(	au)$) across different charge states, linking the observed correlation signatures to the theoretical framework of superradiance and incoherent pumping.
why_interesting: This work provides an experimental realization of superradiance in an electrically driven, non-equilibrium solid-state system, allowing the study of collective quantum emission phenomena typically reserved for cavity QED or cold atom setups.

Partially Pumped Collective Emitters.note: The observation of superradiant photon statistics in an electrically driven system, particularly the dependence of correlations on doping regimes, directly relates to the physics of collective emission from a system where the excitation source or local environment is non-uniform or partially controlled.
